title: delegated-refresh-scheduler-and-async-stream-shim
author: Jordan Kim
release_notes: Added delegated refresh scheduler for long-running streams; introduced async stream shim to smooth cross-SDK parity; bumped python SDK to 0.10.2. No public API breaking changes expected.
description:
Context and motivation: Long-running streaming consumers observed periodic tail-latency spikes when the token refresh path attempted synchronous refreshes while the stream loop held internal locks. This PR introduces a delegated refresh scheduler that decouples credential renewal from the hot path and an async stream shim that provides a lighter-weight async iterator façade for common consumer patterns. The goal is to reduce streaming tail-latency, make token lifecycle behavior observable, and align ergonomics across Python/TS/Go SDKs without changing the core streaming protocol semantics.

What this PR does (single-pass summary):
- Adds a DelegatedRefreshScheduler that runs refreshes on a bounded background worker pool and surfaces a small async-ready lease object to stream sessions.
- Replaces the previous synchronous token refresh path in the streaming client with a non-blocking handoff to the scheduler and a best-effort prefetch for hot sessions.
- Introduces AsyncStreamShim: a compact async iterator wrapper that preserves current message envelopes but yields a simpler consume()/aiter() pattern used in most example apps.
- Exports a lightweight telemetry hook for credential handoffs so ops can wire up metrics (refresh latency, queue depth, failures).
- Adds cross-language interop tests that validate session behavior when the server returns a 401 during an active stream.
- Bumps package version to 0.10.2 and updates changelog.

Checklist (author): [x] design doc linked [x] unit tests [x] e2e smoke tests [x] docs snippet [x] changelog entry

Design notes and tradeoffs: The scheduler delays some refreshes by a few milliseconds to avoid thundering refresh storms when many short-lived streams approach token expiry simultaneously. We intentionally do not make the scheduler an authoritative single source-of-truth for tokens (the transport still validates and can trigger immediate refreshes if needed) to avoid coupling large systems. The AsyncStreamShim is intentionally minimal: it does not introduce buffering beyond the existing client queue and opts for a small allocation/overhead surface to simplify user code.

- feat(shim): implement AsyncStreamShim and examples for aiter()/consume() ergonomics

Review conversation (highlights, chronological):
- Maya: initial review - "Nice separation. Two requests: 1) make the scheduler queue-size configurable via constructor + env var, 2) add a small metric for 'refresh_queue_backpressure' when queue is saturated."
- Jordan (author): "Addressed both: added max_queue size param, env var REDWOOD_SCHED_MAXQ, and an opt-in metric hook. See commit 3/5."
- Liam: "AsyncStreamShim looks good, but can we avoid exposing the internal LeaseHandle on the public stream object? I'd prefer a private attr and a small accessor method to reduce surface area."
- Jordan: "Agreed; replaced direct attr with .credential_lease() accessor and documented intended usage in docs. PTAL."
- Rafal: left a request to tighten unit test determinism around the scheduler's jitter: "replace time.sleep with event loop advance in tests so CI isn't flaky." Jordan updated tests to use freezegun/asyncio loop advance.
- CI: initial run flagged a lint failure (unused import) and a flakey test timeout on the TS interop fixture. Jordan fixed the lint and widened the fixture timeout; rerun succeeded.
- Final approvals: Maya approved after metric hook added; Liam approved after accessor change; Rafal approved after test flake fix.

CI summary: All checks passed on merge. Notable checks:
- unit (py) — pass
- integration (py interop) — pass
- lint/format — pass
- cross-sdk-interop (matrix with TS/Go mocks) — pass
- perf-smoke (light) — pass with ~9% reduction in 99th percentile tail for the streaming benchmark in the mocked harness.

Backwards compatibility: Public client surface remains stable. The scheduler and shim are additive. Consumers that were relying on synchronous refresh side-effects (rare) may observe slightly earlier returns from their streaming recv loops; guidance added to docs on how to await lease completion if deterministic ordering is required.

Versioning and release: Bumped Python SDK to 0.10.2. No coordinated release is required for TS/Go, but interop tests indicate older TS/Go clients remain compatible; we added a small note in the TS/Go SDKs' changelogs to call out the lease accessor if they want to opt-in to the scheduler telemetry.

Merge outcome: Squash-and-merged into main. Post-merge actions: open follow-up to instrument K8s rollout with refresh queue metrics (ENG-3220) and a compatibility test that runs real TS/Go clients against the scheduler in a canary environment.

Related work: ENG-2419 (stream resiliency), ENG-3220 (telemetry for cred system).
